items.q: Fill up: The target glucose in DKD management is set above ______ mg/dl to avoid the risk of hypoglycemia (as printed on the page).
items.exp: Target glucose: >7 mg/dl (to avoid risk of hypoglycemia) — printed exactly as such on the page. (Book p817)

items.q: For DM control and weight loss, the DOC is:
opts: Insulin as the preferred DOC (early in disease)
Glipizide as the DOC for CKD
items.exp: DM control and weight loss: lifestyle modification; DOC: metformin if GFR >30 ml/min. (Book p817)

items.q: Metformin is the DOC when GFR exceeds:
items.exp: DOC: metformin if GFR >30 ml/min. (Book p817)

items.q: For macrovascular complications (CKD/ASCVD), the DOC class is:
The four SGLT2 inhibitors named are:
items.exp: Canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin; initiated at GFR >30 ml/min. (Book p817)

items.q: All but one are SGLT2 inhibitors on the macrovascular list. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Listed: canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin. (Book p817)

items.q: SGLT2 inhibitors for macrovascular complications are initiated when GFR exceeds:
In the diabetes-control table, metformin's effect on CKD progression is:
items.exp: Metformin row: progression of CKD — neutral; ASCVD/HF potential benefit; glucose-lowering high; hypoglycemia low; weight neutral. (Book p817)

items.q: In the table, which drug class shows benefit across CKD progression, ASCVD and heart failure?
items.exp: SGLT2 inhibitors row: benefit / benefit / benefit; intermediate glucose-lowering; low hypoglycemia; weight loss. (Book p817)

items.q: GLP-1 receptor agonists in the table show:
opts: Benefit for progression and ASCVD; potential benefit for HF; weight loss
Neutral for progression, with weight gain and low glucose-lowering
Increased HF risk, with weight gain and high glucose-lowering
Benefit for all three, with weight gain and highest glucose-lowering
items.exp: GLP-1 RA row: benefit, benefit, potential benefit, high, low, loss. (Book p817)

items.q: The DPP-4 inhibitor entry carries which heart-failure caution?
items.exp: DPP-4 row: heart failure — potential risk (saxagliptin); progression/ASCVD neutral. (Book p817)

items.q: Thiazolidinediones show an increased heart-failure risk in the table.
opts: False — they are neutral for HF
items.exp: TZD row: heart failure — increased risk; ASCVD — potential benefit (pioglitazone). (Book p817)

items.q: The ASCVD nuance in the TZD row is:
Which two classes show weight gain with a high hypoglycemia risk in the table?
items.exp: Insulin: hypoglycemia high, weight gain; sulfonylureas: high, gain. (Book p817)

items.q: Match the following drug class to its weight effect in the table — 1) Metformin  2) SGLT2 inhibitors  3) Insulin  4) TZDs … A) Loss  B) Gain  C) Neutral
items.exp: Weight: metformin neutral; SGLT2i loss; insulin gain; TZD gain. (Book p817)

items.q: First-line proteinuria control in DKD is:
items.exp: Proteinuria control: 1st line — SGLT2 (-), ACE (-). (Book p817)

items.q: If proteinuria is uncontrolled with 1st line therapy, the 2nd line drug is:
opts: Finerenone — a non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
Spironolactone — a steroidal MRA of the same class
items.exp: 2nd line uncontrolled with 1st line: finerenone — non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist. (Book p817)

items.q: With finerenone, serum potassium must be monitored because of hyperkalemia risk.
A diabetic CKD patient on SGLT2i + ACEi still has heavy proteinuria. The next agent per the page is:
opts: Add an ARB to the ACE inhibitor
Add a loop diuretic for the edema
Add a DPP-4 inhibitor for glucose
items.exp: 2nd line (uncontrolled with 1st line): finerenone; monitor s. K⁺ (hyperkalemia risk). (Book p817)
